target_customer: Insights and marketing teams at consumer brands that buy qualitative research
problem: Traditional focus groups and interview studies take one to two months and cost $20k or more, so brands test few ideas.
business_model: Per-project and subscription fees for AI-moderated qualitative research studies
product_category: AI market research and consumer insights

founders.name: Sean Conley
founders.background_notes: Product management and growth roles launching AI tools; early career researcher at GiveWell.

founders.name: Sam Stoll
founders.background_notes: Former Palantir software engineer; friends with Conley since Oxford.

competitors.name: Outset
competitors.what: AI-moderated interviews for enterprise research teams

competitors.name: Listen Labs
competitors.what: End to end AI research platform with recruitment, moderation and analysis

competitors.name: Strella
competitors.what: AI-moderated interviews with fast thematic analysis

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs reliable real-time video interviewing with an LLM moderator, participant recruitment and multilingual analysis; hard parts are moderation quality and fraud control, but the building blocks were commodity APIs in 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded rivals sell the same workflow; stickiness would come from panel access, brand relationships and accumulated study history.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to tell; vendor comparison pages from 2026 show a crowded AI-moderated research field.

market_need_then: Brands paid $20k or more and waited weeks for focus groups, while LLMs made automated moderation of video interviews feasible in 2025.

branding.domain_note: Uses motives.ai; no source on how it was acquired.

identity.logo: Wordmark lockup in dark and white versions
identity.voice_and_tone: Energetic and direct: 'Real qual, really fast for consumer-obsessed brands' and 'Dive deeper. Decide faster.'

brand_strength.rationale: The site lists large named customers, but no press or community evidence about the brand itself was found; a real word name overlaps with many unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Motives joined YC in Summer 2025 as a London based team of AI agents running consumer focus groups. It is early and still active, with named brand customers on its site but no verified funding or revenue figures. The timing tailwind from capable LLM moderators is clear, while a crowded set of funded rivals is the main risk.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (VCBacked, CB Insights, Neuronfeed) report a roughly $500K pre-seed around 2025-09 from Y Combinator, Rebel Fund and Davidovs Venture Collective, and one lists $900K total; no press release found, so no round is recorded. A Caplight listing with $565M raised is clearly wrong. One directory says the company was formerly BTRT; unverified. Competitor sources are 2026 vendor comparison pages with no dates near founding, so source_date is null and traction is not stated. Competitor source_date 2026 is the date of the comparison pages, after the 2025 founding, so contemporaneousness is weak.
